featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolute lifesavers – Wild Vets Bandra gave my cat Mao Singh a second chance at life!

I can’t thank the team at Wild Vets in Bandra enough**

A few weeks ago, my beloved feline Mao Singh (my ginger-white drama queen) suddenly became critically ill – lethargic, not eating, and hiding all day. I rushed her to Wild Vets and from the moment we walked in, I knew she was in the best hands.
Dr. Nidhi immediately took charge — calm, thorough, and incredibly compassionate. They didn’t waste a second: full in-house blood work, urine analysis, stroke checks (I think they meant biochemistry/profile), and ultrasound (USG) were all done under one roof on the spot. No running around to different labs, no waiting days for results – everything was diagnosed and treated the same day. That comprehensive in-house facility literally saved precious time and, I genuinely believe, saved Mao Singh’s life. Within hours they had her on IV fluids, targeted medication, and close monitoring.
The entire staff was outstanding — special shoutout to Bhaskar and the rest of the assistants who handled my stressed-out cat with so much gentleness and care, keeping me updated every step of the way, even after hours. The clinic is spotless, well-equipped (dedicated cat consult room, ultrasound room, pharmacy stocked with premium medicines), and clearly designed with pets’ comfort in mind — separate dog den and cat corner to reduce stress.

Yes, Wild Vets is not the cheapest vet in town, but when it’s your family member on the line, quality comes at a price — and it’s worth every single rupee. I’d rather pay for expertise, speed, and state-of-the-art facilities than take risks elsewhere.
Today Mao Singh is back home, eating like a champ, zooming around, and giving me her signature judgmental stares

❤️ Thank you from the bottom of my heart to Dr. Nidhi, Dr. Deb, Bhaskar, and the entire Wild Vets family. You didn’t just treat my cat — you gave her (and me) hope and a future. Forever grateful. If you love your pet, this is the only place in Bandra (and probably Mumbai) I’d trust blindly.
Highly recommended — 5 stars aren’t enough! 🐱💙

Update on 16/03/26: Wildvets has now demanded Rs. 1 Lakh in defamation & Rs. 25k for their legal fees in sending me a civil court summon for an honest & truthful review of their practice.

Requesting all pet parents to be extremely cautious while approaching such an establishment.

I have an ongoing treatment for 2 of my cats- there is no doubt that there is  quite of a lot of immoral practice.

21/06/25 - Took my cat “Honey” with a complain of blood in his urine. Drs prescribed a stool, urine, radiograph, & blood test; we agreed & did the radiograph & blood test right there.

Radiograph received on 21st itself, with missing diagnosis that their drs insist we can’t read

Blood reports were a nightmare to get - first admin staff keeps insisting that they’ve sent it over email. I’m receiving other emails from them, they also have the correct email so I guessed it’s some tech issue & requested if she can whatsapp instead. The sheer arrogance of this woman. Downright refusing to do so; Wildvets never gives a hard copy of their reports, & this person is refusing to share it over whatsapp, how am I supposed to see the results? After much arguing she finally agreed to share over whatsapp - what she shares is a stool report from 2024; keep in mind I sent a blood sample in 2025. Explaining her this was another mountain to climb.

23rd - I took my cats Honey and Cream for a sono as Cream also started to show some issues. They did their sono at the clinic itself, in the morning. As of now - 24th June evening - I’m yet to see these reports, keep in mind most places (human or animal) produce these in less than an hour. On 23rd I was told these reports will come by the evening, now I’m being told it will take 3 DAYS?

To top this, their drs injected both my cats with meds their team REFUSED to write down. After we asked the receptionist why so, she exclaimed that all this is in their system. Basically to trap you from going to other vets. Till date I have not recvd a written prescription of what was administered to them. Imagine going to a hospital & them injecting you with whatever, then refusing to disclose? Where is the transparency? Does this not smell of malpractice?

Their drs, despite so many days have been unable to give a clear explanation. Upon seeing the cat’s sono at the clinic they claimed “one was worse than the other”, I’m sorry these educated professionals are calling “worse than the other” a diagnosis? Till date not one of them has explained what results came out of the urinary or stool test. Their drs are always in a rush for “lunch” or “meeting”, I understand prior commitments, but it takes 5 mins to get on a call & explain.

I have so far spent upwards of 25k at their clinic and yet have 0 clear diagnosis, no physical reports (how am I supposed to show radiograph & sono to other drs? On a mobile screen? Or print on a paper? What does wild vets charge a premium for if a report cannot be printed & given? How poor is this place?god only knows how long will the sono take.

I am speaking with 2 other external vets, both of them appalled at Wild Vet’s behavior. Keep in mind I’m not even paying these drs & they have managed to chart a treatment plan, something wild vets is still unable to do. All we do here is x no. of tests to crank up the bill, with drs giving 0 explanations, admin staff disrespecting you at every chance they get, & a potential malpractice of injecting animals with substances that can make their situation worse. They won’t let you take a simple file to store prescription without paying for it, but they will ensure to milk you dry out of money until your wallet dies or your pet.

I’m sure Wildvets will have a long defensive answer to give, I’m keen on knowing what justifies rudeness, lack of communication, & refusal to write down administered meds

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

featured_reviews.name: sms sweta
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a pet parent, I’m sure many of you will understand the kind of fear and helplessness we feel when something isn’t right with our baby. I went through exactly that when my 14-year-old feline, Goldie, was diagnosed with a serious tumour on her left paw. Those days were filled with worry, questions, and uncertainty.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

I must admit, I was initially skeptical about traveling all the way from the suburbs to Bandra for treatment — but today, I can say with complete conviction that every visit, every effort, was absolutely worth it.

What touched me deeply was that even after a month, Dr. Pratyush personally followed up to check on Goldie’s health. That level of care is rare and speaks volumes about the kind of people they are — not just doctors, but true lifesavers.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

featured_reviews.name: Smitaa Nair
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a blessing. My German shepherd champ was taken to super pets in an emergency situation. He had developed something called GDV. I was unaware if this situation being a pet parent since more than 17 years now (I have had pets since several years) After taking him to vetic hospital for emergency (which was extremely careless and didn’t even treat it like emergency) post his X-ray on recommendation from some friends I rushed him to super pets. They immediately took charge of the situation. He underwent operation and was discharged in 5 days. We had to take him for regular follow ups and on a follow up in a weeks time, doctors suspected something wrong and again on further tests discovered that his spleen had got affected and damaged along with few further conditions that had developed. He underwent second surgery. He battled for his life for a month in this hospital. He was hospitalised. The care, affection and love he recieved along with the proper medical care is nothing less than a gift for parents seeing their child fight for life and death each day. Inspite of he being aggressive he was pampered and taken care of as if he belongs to them. His entire body had collapsed and post 1 month he finally got discharged. He had lost his ability to walk post all this condition as his hip and spine had got affected. We continued Physio with them. It’s October today. My boy got discharged in June and we are in our way for our regular Physio all hail and hearty, not just walking but running and bullying my other 2 dogs :) No words can thank them enough. His recovery is nothing less than a miracle only because of timely care and attention given to him by the super vets at super pets.
